stem.en: Sameer's ₹500 earned ₹40 in its first year at 8% a year. He leaves the whole ₹540 in for a second year at the same rate. How much interest does the second year add?

text.en: ₹40, because the rate has not changed and the money he put in is still ₹500.
₹43.20, because the second year's 8% is worked out on ₹540 and not on ₹500.
₹80, because two years at 8% on the same ₹500 must give ₹40 in each of the years.
₹3.20, because that is what the second year adds over and above the first year's interest.

explanation.en: The second year starts from the ₹540 that was in the scheme after year one, so 8% of ₹540 = ₹43.20. The ₹3.20 is the difference between the two years' interest - the amount that year one's ₹40 earned in year two - not the second year's interest itself. This is why interest that stays in keeps growing.

hints.en: Ask what amount the 8% is calculated on at the start of the second year.
8% of ₹540 is more than 8% of ₹500. The extra is the first year's interest earning something itself.
